title: Injective-term subset Cech augmentation is monic on homology
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, $V=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$ and $D_S=D(\prod_{j\in S}f_j)$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary unbounded cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $K,T$ be complexes of $A$-modules, with degreewise $A$-linear isomorphisms $\sigma_n:K^n\cong\Gamma(V,J^n)$ and $\tau_n:T^n\cong\prod_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)}\Gamma(D_S,J^{n+1-|S|})$. Assume $\sigma$ identifies the differential of $K$ with the sectionwise differential of $J$, and $\tau$ identifies the differential of $T$ with the signed total formula: at $S$ its vertical term is $(-1)^{|S|-1}d_J$ and its horizontal term is the sum over $j\in S$ of restriction from $D_{S\setminus\{j\}}$, multiplied by $(-1)^{|\{i\in S:i<j\}|}$, with empty deletions zero. All coefficient degrees are transported by their displayed integer equalities. Let $\alpha:K\to T$ be a chain map which under these coordinates is restriction from $V$ on singleton coordinates and zero on all larger subsets. The open inclusion inequalities and degree equalities in the Lean signature specify only the transports in these formulas. Assume in addition that each $J^n$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then $H^n(\alpha)$ is injective for every integer $n$. No K-injectivity or boundedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Sheaf separatedness proves the augmentation injective in each degree, by evaluating on singletons and transporting the degree equality back via naturality. This also handles the empty cover.

Induct on the number of possible positive columns. Apply the single-column cancellation at each successor step; subtracting a total boundary preserves the differential because d squared is zero. Every subset has cardinality at most r, so this induction reduces any primitive whose differential has no positive Cech coordinates to a singleton-supported primitive with the same differential.
The singleton-supported primitive glues to an augmented section. The chain-map identity and degreewise injectivity identify the differential of that section with the original source element.

Lift a homology element to cycles using the surjectivity of homology projection. If its image is zero, the opcycles quotient criterion supplies a total primitive. Apply the elementwise boundary lift just proved; the source opcycles class is zero, hence its homology class is zero by injectivity of homology inclusion. This proves monicity of the homology map.
